references.text: Moses' song at the Red Sea asks the same question, 'Who is like you?' regarding the Lord's incomparable power to save His people.
Blessing upon the people who have the Lord as their God, parallel to 'Blessed are you, Israel.'
The Lord is described as Israel's help and shield, using the same imagery as 'the shield that helps you.'
Blessing upon the people who have the Lord as their God.
The promise to tread on the heights of the land, parallel to 'you shall tread upon their high places.'
The question, 'Who is a God like you?' concerning the Lord's unique ability to forgive and save.
The Lord gives strength to tread on the heights, using the same imagery of victory over enemies.
Paul asks, 'If God is for us, who can be against us?' - expressing the same thought about God's incomparable protection of His people.
The promise that believers will trample Satan under their feet, parallel to victory over enemies.
